meta.title: Everstead for Business | Advisers, solicitors, care providers, employers
meta.description: For advisers, solicitors, care providers and employers: one secure place for the documents that pass between you and the people you serve. Hold none of it.

hero.title: One secure place for the documents that pass between you.
hero.sub: Send a contract straight into someone's own vault. Ask for one proof of address and see that item alone, for as long as you need it. They keep everything, including after they leave you.
hero.ctaSecondary: See the four ways we work

audiences.title: Four ways Everstead fits an organisation.

items.title: Financial advisers and wealth managers
items.body: See how prepared each client's family really is: a readiness score, a document review queue and requests, all on the client's consent. The conversation moves from have you done it to your family can find it.

items.title: Solicitors and will writers
items.body: The will settles the law. Everstead is where the family learns where it is, who to call and what to do first. Clients who arrive organised make probate faster, and your firm is the one who gave them the tool.

items.title: Care homes and care providers
items.body: Families arrive at admission without the details your team needs, and staff carry the questions when a resident dies. Hand every family a free plan and a one page Emergency Pack. Nothing to buy, nothing stored by the home.

items.title: Employers, HR and benefits teams
items.body: Bereavement and caring take people out for months, not days. Offer a benefit that gets the practical side in order before it is needed, free for the employee, with no employee data held by the employer.

items.title: The family actually uses it
items.body: Most of this category is a document someone signs and files. Everstead is a living plan: reminders when something expires, an annual check, family sharing with private spaces. It is still there in five years.

items.title: You are not holding the data
items.body: The vault belongs to the person, not to your organisation. Advisers and solicitors see only what a client has shared. A care home or an employer sees nothing at all, so no new data duty lands on you.

items.title: It starts free
items.body: No card and no contract for the family. You can hand it out to every client, resident or employee on the day of the meeting, which is the only moment anyone ever acts.

how.title: Three steps, and the family keeps control.

steps.title: You introduce it
steps.body: A link, a card in the folder, a QR code on a welcome pack, or a word at the right moment. The family starts free and adds one thing at a time.

steps.title: They decide what you see
steps.body: Nothing reaches an organisation until the person chooses it. Advisers and solicitors get a portal. Care providers and employers never hold the data at all.

steps.title: We keep it alive
steps.body: Expiry reminders, an annual review, a nudge when something important is missing. The plan is still current long after the meeting.

trust.title: What every partner can say to the people they serve.
points: UK company, vaults hosted in London under UK GDPR
Free plan with no card, export and deletion at any time
Emergency access opens only after a human check
No advertising profiles, no selling of data

next.title: From a plan for one day to a place people use every month.
next.body: Everstead already holds the documents a family will need. The next step is the ones that arrive while everyone is very much alive: an organisation sending a contract or a certificate straight into someone's vault, and a person granting time limited access to an ID or a proof of address instead of emailing a scan. Same vault, same consent model.

items.title: Send a document to a member's vault
items.body: Your organisation pushes a document to someone by email address. They accept once, and it lands in a vault they own and keep when they leave.

items.title: Time limited sharing, the other way
items.body: A person grants read access to exactly the items you need, for as long as you need them, and it expires on its own.

next.note: Neither is live yet. We are choosing the first partner organisations to build them with.

final.title: Tell us who you serve.
final.body: Twenty minutes with the founding team is enough to see whether Everstead fits your clients, residents or employees, and what a pilot would look like.
final.note: We are working personally with our first partner organisations.

meta.title: Everstead for Solicitors and Will Writers | A plan the family can follow
meta.description: The will is drafted. Everstead is where the family learns where it is, who to call and what to do first. Free for your clients to start, with nothing held by your firm.

hero.title: The will is signed. The family still does not know where anything is.
hero.sub: You write the instrument that settles an estate. Everstead holds everything around it: the accounts, the policies, the people to call, and the line that says where the original will is kept. Your clients start free, and your firm holds nothing.

problem.title: What most clients leave behind is a document, not a map.

items.title: The will gets filed and forgotten
items.body: Clients tell nobody where the original is. Executors open drawers, ring three firms, and sometimes try to apply for probate on a photocopy.

items.title: Assets go missing
items.body: A dormant account, a policy nobody knew about, a crypto wallet, a subscription that keeps billing. The estate you administer is only as complete as what the family can find.

items.title: Probate takes longer than it should
items.body: Every missing statement is a letter, a wait, and a chargeable hour the family resents paying for.

offer.title: Something to hand over at signing.

items.title: Somewhere to record where the will is
items.body: The firm, the reference and the storage location, so the executor starts with your details instead of a search.

items.title: A complete asset picture
items.body: Accounts, property, policies, pensions, digital assets and subscriptions, kept current by the client rather than reconstructed after a death.

items.title: An executor who is ready
items.body: The client names their executor inside Everstead. When the time comes, that person gets a guided checklist instead of a shoebox.

items.title: Your firm stays the first call
items.body: You can be listed as the family's professional contact, so the call comes to you. Nothing is stored on your side and no new data duty falls on the firm.

how.title: Three steps, and the client keeps control.

steps.title: Hand it over at signing
steps.body: A link or a card in the folder with the will. The client starts free, no card required.

steps.title: They fill it in over time
steps.body: One thing at a time, with reminders. Most people add the important half in a single sitting.

steps.title: The executor is guided
steps.body: Emergency access opens after a human check, and the executor gets a step by step list that starts with your firm.

items.a: No. Everstead is an organisation tool, not a legal service. It records where the will is and everything around it. The instrument you draft is still the only thing that decides the estate.

items.q: You publish a free will template. Does that compete with me?
items.a: It is a simple template for people who would otherwise die intestate, and every page of it says that anything beyond the simplest estate needs a solicitor. The people it reaches were not going to instruct a firm. The ones who read it and realise their situation is not simple are told to come to you.

items.q: What does my firm have to hold?
items.a: Nothing. No integration, no data processing agreement, no client record on your side, unless you take the adviser portal, which is a separate arrangement.

items.q: Where is the data actually held?
items.a: In London, on Amazon Web Services, under UK GDPR. Everstead is a UK-registered company and the contents of a vault do not leave the UK. The site itself is served from a global network, and every supporting service we use is named on our subprocessors page.

final.title: See it with one of your own client files in mind.
final.body: Twenty minutes with the founding team. We will show you what a client sees, what an executor sees, and exactly what your firm would and would not hold.

hero.eyebrow: For care homes and care providers

problem.title: Three moments where the paperwork lands on staff.

items.title: Admission
items.body: Next of kin, the GP, power of attorney, funeral wishes, the pharmacy, the solicitor. Half of it arrives late and the rest arrives as a phone call.

items.title: A sudden decline
items.body: The family that has to decide quickly is the family that does not know whether there is an advance decision, or where it is kept.

items.title: After a death
items.body: Staff field questions about accounts, subscriptions and belongings for weeks, with no authority to answer any of them.

offer.title: Two things to give every family, both free.

items.title: The one page Emergency Pack
items.body: A printable page with the numbers, the names and the wishes that matter. The family fills it in, keeps a copy in the resident's room and one in a pocket.

items.title: A free family plan
items.body: Everything else lives in the family's own vault: documents, accounts, wishes, trusted people. Nothing to buy, no card required.

items.title: Nothing held by the home
items.body: You never store, process or become responsible for any of it. There is no integration and no agreement to sign.

items.title: An answer at the hardest moment
items.body: When a family asks your staff what they should be doing, there is something calm and practical to say instead of an apology.

steps.title: Put it in the welcome pack
steps.body: A card with a link and a QR code, handed over at admission with the rest of the paperwork.

steps.title: Families set it up themselves
steps.body: In their own time, on their own phone. Your team administers nothing.

steps.title: Use it when it matters
steps.body: At a care review, during a decline, or after a death, the family already has the answers in one place.

items.q: Does the home hold any resident data?
items.a: No. The vault belongs to the family. We give you printed material and a link, and nothing flows back to the home.

items.q: What does it cost the home?
items.a: Nothing to hand it out. If you want branded material, a briefing for staff or a group arrangement across several homes, that is a conversation.

items.q: Is it suitable for residents living with dementia?
items.a: It is usually the family or the attorney who fills it in, which is exactly who needs it. The Emergency Pack works on paper for anyone who prefers paper.

items.q: Where is the data actually held?
items.a: In London, on Amazon Web Services, under UK GDPR. Everstead is a UK-registered company and the contents of a vault do not leave the UK. The site itself is served from a global network, and every supporting service we use is named on our subprocessors page.

final.title: Ask for the Emergency Pack.
final.body: We will send the printable pack and a short briefing for your team, and show you what a family sees. No cost and no obligation.

meta.title: Everstead for Employers, HR and Benefits Teams | Documents you never have to hold
meta.description: Send a contract into an employee's own secure vault. Ask for a proof of address and see that one item, for as long as you need it. Nothing in an inbox, nothing on your drive.

hero.eyebrow: For employers, HR and benefits teams
hero.title: Your people's documents, without you having to hold them.
hero.sub: Send a contract straight into someone's own secure vault. Ask for a proof of address and see that one item, for as long as you need it. Nothing sits in an inbox, nothing sits on your drive, and what you send stays theirs after they leave.

problem.title: Most employee documents end up somewhere nobody chose.

items.title: Scans in inboxes
items.body: A photograph of a passport sent by email is still there years later: in their sent folder, in yours, and in whatever was backed up along the way. Nobody decided that. It just happened.

items.title: Drives nobody prunes
items.body: Onboarding folders keep right to work documents and bank details long after the reason for holding them has gone. That is not a filing habit, it is a breach waiting to be found.

items.title: And what you send goes missing
items.body: Contracts, pension summaries, certificates. Sent once, lost with a laptop, and asked for again three years later at the worst possible moment.

offer.title: A place for both directions, that you do not own.

items.title: Send it into a vault they own
items.body: The document lands in their own secure place rather than an attachment. They keep it when they leave you, which is also why they bother to keep it at all.

items.title: Ask for one item, for a while
items.body: They grant you sight of exactly the document you asked for, for the days you asked for. It stops on its own, so nothing lingers because somebody forgot to tidy up.

items.title: Hold none of it
items.body: You never see, store or process what is in anyone's vault. A sensitive category of data leaves your systems, and with it a set of obligations you carry today.

items.title: And it is there on the worst day too
items.body: The same vault holds what a family needs if an employee dies or has to care for someone. That is where Everstead started, and it is still why people keep it once they have it.

how.title: One email, then it runs itself.

steps.title: We give you the material
steps.body: Copy for an email or an intranet post, and a link. You send it.

steps.title: People accept once
steps.body: The first document you send is accepted by the person, and that is what connects you. Everything you send after that files itself.

steps.title: You see delivery, never content
steps.body: Every exchange leaves a timestamped receipt you can file. It shows what was sent, to whom, and when it was answered, and nothing at all about what is in their vault.

next.title: Every document that passes between you, not only the first one.
next.body: An employee's vault is the natural place for the paperwork that passes between you: a contract, a certificate, an attestation. And the same vault can answer the questions you ask at onboarding, without a scan sitting in an inbox forever.

items.title: Send a document to an employee's vault
items.body: You push a document by email address. The employee accepts once, and it lands in a vault they own and keep after they leave.

items.title: Onboarding, the other way round
items.body: An employee grants read access to exactly the items you need, an ID, a proof of address, a next of kin, for as long as you need them. Then it expires on its own.

next.note: Neither is live yet. We are choosing the first employers to build them with, so say so on the call if that is the part you want.

items.a: The copies. Right to work documents, proof of address, bank details, certificates: you see them when you need them and you do not keep them afterwards. The original stays with the person it belongs to.

items.q: Do we become responsible for the data?
items.a: No. The relationship over the data is between the employee and Everstead. Your organisation is neither a controller nor a processor of anything in the vault.
Nothing, if you only want to hand out the free plan. A paid arrangement covers the whole team and the material around a launch. We work that out per organisation on the call.

items.q: How is this different from an employee assistance programme?
items.a: An assistance programme is counselling and advice. This is the practical layer: the documents that pass between you, and the ones a family needs if the worst happens. Most employers who take this run both.
